clue.text: Composer to play jazz in West African nation with Englishman (one who's extremely attractive)

indicators.note: one piece is placed inside the name of the country, so the country's letters wrap around it

parts.note: Benin is a country on the Gulf of Guinea
jazz musicians jam when they improvise together
a Brit is a native of Britain
a perfect ten scores top marks for looks

explanation.surface: A composer seems to be jamming in West Africa alongside a charming Englishman.
explanation.walkthrough: Calling someone 'a ten' means they score top marks for looks, a perfect score out of ten.
explanation.definitionFit: Benjamin Britten was the English composer of Peter Grimes and the War Requiem.

clue.text: Admired sib, potentially?!

indicators.note: potentially points to what the letters could become once rearranged

parts.note: the letters of these two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A sister who is looked up to might well end up attending the bride.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: a beloved sister is a likely choice to attend at a wedding.
explanation.definitionFit: A bride's sister is often chosen as one of her attendants at the wedding.

clue.text: Concealed in ultra-Ponzi return without value

indicators.note: a return goes back the other way, so the hidden letters are read right to left
something concealed in a phrase sits inside its letters

parts.note: the last two letters of ultra and first three of Ponzi

explanation.surface: A fraudulent super-Ponzi scheme pays out a worthless return.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Return' looks like investment income, matching the Ponzi surface, but it signals reading backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: No-par stock is issued with no stated face value printed on the certificate.

clue.text: Take a little off the top of taller heart doctor

indicators.text: Take a little off the top
indicators.note: like a light haircut, a small piece is trimmed from the start of the word

parts.note: its first letter is cut
the heart of a matter is its gist

explanation.surface: A barber's request to trim a tall cardiologist's hair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heart doctor' looks like one unit, a cardiologist, but 'heart' belongs to the wordplay and 'doctor' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An allergist is a physician who specialises in allergies, a kind of medical doctor.

clue.text: Along with you and all of us, I make myself heard for this

definitions.text: Along with you and all of us, I make myself heard for this

parts.words: Along with you and all of us, I make myself heard for this
parts.note: surface reading: a speaker joining a crowd to demand something
setter's reading: the rhyme 'I scream, you scream, we all scream for' a frozen treat

explanation.walkthrough: The clue paraphrases the old American jingle 'I scream, you scream, we all scream for' a frozen dessert, whose punchline is that 'I scream' sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The jingle names a frozen dairy dessert as the thing everyone shouts for.

clue.text: Happen to risk money on an unfinished thought

indicators.note: an unfinished word stops short, so its final letter is dropped

parts.note: to bet is to wager money on an outcome
an idea is a thought; it loses its last letter

explanation.surface: Gambling on a half-formed hunch, hoping it comes true.
explanation.definitionFit: Betide is an old verb meaning to befall or occur, as in 'woe betide'.

clue.text: Playwright heads off into bar scene every night

indicators.note: the heads of words are their first letters, taken off and gathered

parts.note: initial letters of the five words

explanation.surface: A dramatist heads off to the bars every night of the week.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heads off' looks like 'sets out', but it asks for the first letters of the words that follow.
explanation.definitionFit: Henrik Ibsen was the Norwegian dramatist who wrote A Doll's House and Hedda Gabler.

clue.text: Around beginning of October, deceptive Lotto ads mushroom

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go around the single letter taken from the month
something deceptive misleads by disguise, so the letters are disguised in a new order

parts.note: the letters of these two words are rearranged

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter

parts.note: first letter of the month

explanation.surface: Misleading lottery adverts multiply rapidly around October.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mushroom' looks like a verb, to spread fast, but it is the noun being defined.
explanation.definitionFit: A toadstool is a mushroom, especially an inedible or poisonous one.

clue.text: Afternoon is ______ for Chomsky

wordplay.note: after noon, it is no longer morning

explanation.surface: A fill-in-the-blank: a fact about the afternoon, phrased for a linguist.
explanation.walkthrough: AM is the abbreviation for morning (ante meridiem), so after midday there is NO AM.
explanation.definitionFit: The blank asks for the linguist Chomsky's first name, which is Noam.

clue.text: I plus me: perverse desire

indicators.note: something perverse goes against the normal order, so the letters before it are rearranged

parts.note: the letters of these three words are the raw material

explanation.surface: A self-absorbed equation: myself and me add up to a twisted longing.
explanation.definitionFit: An impulse is a sudden urge or wish to act, a kind of desire.

clue.text: Drunkard returns and — voila! — Mexican food

indicators.note: returning means going back the way one came, so the word for a drunkard is read from right to left

parts.note: a sot is a habitual drunk
ta-da is the flourish that accompanies a reveal, just like voila

explanation.surface: A drunk comes back and, with a flourish, produces a Mexican dish.
explanation.definitionFit: A tostada is a crisp fried tortilla with toppings, a staple of Mexican cuisine.

clue.text: Herr Rorschach reveals a feature of this clue

parts.note: surface reading: the inkblot psychologist uncovering a trait, as his test claims to
setter's reading: the run of letters straddling the two words is a misspelling with one R too many, so the clue really does contain a mistake

explanation.surface: The inkblot psychologist diagnoses something about the very clue you are reading.
explanation.walkthrough: Read across the gap in 'Herr Rorschach' and you find the answer spelt with three Rs in a row: the slip is itself the feature the clue points to.
explanation.definitionFit: A clue containing a misspelt word has a mistake in it, so a blunder is truly one of its features.

clue.text: Send user off with bad customer service, perhaps

indicators.note: something off is out of order or gone wrong, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters of these two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A help desk brushes off a user, the hallmark of poor customer care.
explanation.definitionFit: Impoliteness is one example of poor service, which the 'perhaps' acknowledges.

clue.text: Fat around the neck is toast?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a fold of flab beneath the jaw
second meaning, playfully: the drinking salute 'chin-chin' says chin twice

explanation.walkthrough: 'Chin-chin' is a jaunty drinking toast, so a doubled chin is, punningly, a toast; the question mark flags the joke.
explanation.definitionFit: A fleshy fold beneath the jaw is this; the toast 'chin-chin' is the same word said twice.

clue.text: Consider possible gain in a second shot

parts.note: to mull something over is to consider it

indicators.note: a possible version is one of several arrangements, so the letters of the next word can be reordered

parts.note: these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Sounds like a gambler weighing up the odds of winning on a second attempt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Consider possible gain' reads like a financial phrase, but it splits as a verb plus a reshuffled word.
explanation.definitionFit: In casual golf, a mulligan is an extra stroke allowed after a poor one, so a free retry.

clue.text: Engineer led outing a certain distance from Greenwich

indicators.note: to engineer is to construct or rework, so the letters are rebuilt in a new order

parts.note: the letters of these two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: An engineer leads a field trip some way out from Greenwich.
explanation.walkthrough: Greenwich, in London, sits on the prime meridian, the zero line for east-west angles on the globe.
explanation.definitionFit: Longitude measures angular distance east or west of the prime meridian through Greenwich.

clue.text: Korean dictator with Yoko's robe

parts.note: the Kim dynasty has ruled North Korea
Yoko Ono, artist and widow of John Lennon

explanation.surface: A North Korean leader wearing a garment belonging to Yoko Ono.
explanation.definitionFit: A kimono is a long, wide-sleeved Japanese robe tied with a sash.

clue.text: Blowing up in notable New York building without resistance

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: without means lacking, so one letter is taken out of the building's name

parts.note: the wedge-shaped Flatiron Building in Manhattan
R is the physics symbol for resistance; this letter is removed

explanation.surface: Something exploding inside a famous Manhattan skyscraper, meeting no resistance.
explanation.definitionFit: Inflation is the act of filling something with air so it swells up.

clue.text: Chopped up conifers should be usable in court

indicators.note: chopping up breaks something into pieces that can be reassembled differently

parts.note: the letters of this word are rearranged

explanation.surface: Felled pine trees could serve as evidence at a trial.
explanation.definitionFit: Forensic describes evidence or methods suitable for legal proceedings.

clue.text: Shaken, I get in light

indicators.note: shaking jumbles the contents, so the letters that follow are mixed up

parts.note: the letters of these three words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone rattled after getting into a lit room or vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: To light a fire or fuse is to set it burning, which is to kindle it.

clue.text: Beat back and forth with iron, for example

indicators.note: going back means reading the word for beat from right to left

parts.note: to flog is to beat; read backwards here
a second word for beat, this time read forwards

explanation.surface: Pressing clothes with an iron, pushing it back and forth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beat' is used twice: one synonym reads backwards and another reads forwards, as 'back and forth' suggests. The surface conjures ironing laundry.
explanation.definitionFit: An iron is one kind of stick used on the golf course, alongside woods, wedges and putters.

clue.text: Coming up some other time with dumpling

indicators.note: in a down entry, coming up means reading from bottom to top

parts.note: 'not now' means some other time

explanation.surface: Putting off a dumpling meal until another day.
explanation.definitionFit: A wonton is a small Chinese filled dumpling, often served in soup.

clue.text: Figure out what's wrong with San Diego in turmoil

indicators.note: turmoil is confusion and disorder, so the city's letters are jumbled

parts.note: the letters of the California city are rearranged

explanation.surface: A troubleshooter working out what is ailing a California city in chaos.
explanation.definitionFit: To diagnose is to identify the cause of a problem, as a doctor or mechanic does.

clue.text: Leader of gorillas and tailless monkeys looks in amazement

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

parts.note: first letter of the word
apes are primates without tails, playfully described as tailless monkeys

explanation.surface: Zoo visitors stare open-mouthed at the gorilla troop's leader and the apes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tailless monkeys' tempts you to cut a letter from a word for monkeys; instead it is a cheeky description of apes, which have no tails.
explanation.definitionFit: To gape is to stare with mouth open, as people do when astonished.

clue.text: Exchange in front of tree yields plenty

indicators.note: swapping the letters at the front of the word rearranges it

parts.note: the maple is a tree

explanation.surface: A trade-off in front of a tree produces abundance, like a market under an orchard.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the first two letters of the tree swap places; the rest stay put.
explanation.definitionFit: Ample means more than enough, which is the sense of plenty as an adjective.

clue.text: Announced ordinary aircraft

indicators.note: something announced is spoken out, so the word for ordinary is judged by its sound

parts.note: plain means ordinary

explanation.surface: An airport tannoy calls out an unremarkable flight.
explanation.definitionFit: A plane is an aeroplane, a fixed-wing flying machine.

clue.text: Walk the dog and cat toward the attic

indicators.note: the attic is at the top of the house, so in a down entry the word is read upwards

parts.note: a dog and a cat are household pets

explanation.surface: Household chores: take the dog out and shoo the cat upstairs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Walk the dog' looks like one phrase, but 'Walk' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To step is to walk, moving by lifting and setting down the feet.

clue.text: Behind in holiday broadcast

indicators.note: one piece goes inside another, with the holiday's letters around it

parts.note: Tet is the Vietnamese lunar new year festival
a behind is the backside or rump

explanation.surface: Someone lagging behind during a televised holiday programme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Behind' looks like 'late', but it is the backside. 'Broadcast' is a verb here: to proclaim loudly.
explanation.definitionFit: To trumpet news is to announce it widely and loudly, to spread it about.

clue.text: Turn a crawfish shell for a particular sailor's sustenance

parts.note: a spin is a turn
taken as written

indicators.note: a shell is the outside of the creature, so only the outermost letters of its name are kept

parts.note: first and last letters of the word

explanation.surface: Seafood prep: twisting a crawfish to crack its shell for a sailor's meal.
explanation.walkthrough: The particular sailor is Popeye, the cartoon seaman who gains strength from eating tinned greens.
explanation.definitionFit: The leafy vegetable is famously what gives the cartoon sailor Popeye his strength.

clue.text: Matter of grave importance for dry-cleaning establishment?

definitions.meaning: second meaning, whimsically: a business that irons clothes

explanation.walkthrough: The second half reads the phrase literally: a concern is a business, and pressing is ironing. The question mark flags the pun.
explanation.definitionFit: An urgent problem is a pressing matter; a firm that presses garments is, jokingly, a business of that name.
